headline: Federal Edtech Guidance and a Texas Ransomware Scare Frame a Week of Hard Trade-offs
thesis: EdSurge covers new U.S. Department of Education guidance tying edtech funding to evidence, not just adoption, the same week Inside Higher Ed reports a ransomware attack delayed the start of classes at UT San Antonio and Brookings raises fresh alarms about AI surveillance in schools.
summary: Ed tech's policy conversation sharpens this week as EdSurge reports the U.S. Department of Education has issued its long-awaited Dear Colleague Letter on edtech, urging states to tie purchasing decisions to measurable evidence rather than adoption metrics alone, while singling out Arkansas, Indiana, Louisiana, Michigan and Texas for performance-based contracting models. The guidance lands the same week Inside Higher Ed reports Senate Democrats objecting to a Pentagon-NIH research funding shift, and recaps a ransomware incident that delayed the start of classes at UT San Antonio — a reminder that the cyber-resilience push schools have been building toward all year remains unfinished. Equity concerns keep surfacing in parallel: Brookings warns that AI-powered surveillance tools in schools raise safety and racial-bias concerns even as adoption spreads, and THE Journal covers CoSN's push for screen-time policies that prioritize purpose over blanket restriction. On the classroom-AI front, Ed-Fi reframes its interoperability data standard for an AI-shaped future, EdTech Digest argues for a more intentional, human-centered approach to classroom technology, and EdTech Magazine tracks the AI data trends K-12 leaders are watching for the year ahead. EdSurge itself makes news, adding six journalists and educators — including Washington Post reporter Todd Frankel — to a new advisory board meant to sharpen its coverage of AI in schools. The fall conference calendar keeps filling in behind it all: 1EdTech heads to Thessaloniki for Learning Impact Europe, ISTE+ASCD opens a new Edtech Leader Certification cohort, and THE Journal's Tech Tactics in Education goes virtual on September 23, all ahead of EdTech Week's October return to Columbia and Ed-Fi's November Alliance Summit.
footnote: Compiled from 11 curated edtech sources · September 9, 2026 · Items were sourced and dated via web-search indexing rather than live page fetches this run (direct fetches to source sites were blocked); several sources (Education Technology Insights, Ed-Fi, EdTech Magazine, EdTech Week) had no September-dated coverage surface in search, so their most relevant recent items are listed instead with a note.

arts.s: Brookings finds AI-powered surveillance tools, from weapon-detection cameras to listening devices, are deployed disproportionately in large urban schools serving low-income and minority students.
